title: João Renato Leripio
text:
Forecasting, Statistical Modeling & Data Science


 joao@rleripio.com
 leripiorenato
 leripio
 rleripio.com




Senior data science and modeling professional specializing in forecasting, time series, and complex data. Currently leads the Data Science and Modeling team at Kapitalo, combining hands-on statistical modeling and technical leadership with the development of reliable analytical pipelines and data products.



Modeling: Forecasting · Econometrics · Machine Learning · State-Space Models · Bayesian Inference
Data: Alternative and Unstructured Data · High-Frequency Data · Web Data
Tools & Delivery: R · Stan · Python · SQL · DuckDB · PostgreSQL · dbt · APIs · Git · Reproducible Pipelines · Automated Reporting · Dashboards · Web Applications







Data Science & Economic Modeling Lead


São Paulo, Brazil · 2022–Present



Lead the Data Science and Modeling team within Macroeconomic Research, providing technical direction, mentoring analysts, and overseeing the development of quantitative models and analytical products.
Design forecasting and nowcasting systems for economic variables using time-series methods, high-frequency indicators, and alternative data.
Develop statistical approaches for complex datasets characterized by changing predictors, mixed frequencies, missing observations, and continuously evolving coverage.
Transform web, textual, and other unstructured sources into structured indicators and model inputs for research and decision-making.
Build and maintain end-to-end analytical workflows, including data collection, databases, model estimation, automated reporting, dashboards, and internal applications.
Collaborate with economists and investment professionals to translate open-ended research questions into reliable and interpretable quantitative solutions.






Quantitative Research Analyst


São Paulo, Brazil · 2019–2022



Developed quantitative models, indicators, and forecasting tools for macroeconomic and financial research.
Applied time-series and econometric methods to extract signals from noisy, incomplete, and high-frequency data.
Integrated alternative datasets into recurring macroeconomic and investment research workflows.
Communicated model results and analytical findings to economists and investment professionals.






Economic Research Analyst


Brasília, Brazil · 2017–2019



Conducted applied economic research and monitored regional economic activity using official and administrative data.
Developed statistical indicators and analytical tools to measure economic conditions and support public-policy discussions.
Produced reports and presented quantitative findings to technical and nontechnical audiences.





M.S. in Economics, Universidade Federal Fluminense · 2017
B.S. in Economics, Universidade Federal Fluminense · 2013



Author of R for Economic Research, a practical guide to data workflows, statistical modeling, time series, and forecasting for applied research. The book has received more than 50,000 views from readers in over 50 countries.




Nowcasting When Predictors Keep Changing: Leveraging Cross-Sectional Information in High-Dimensional, High-Turnover Data — International Symposium on Forecasting · Montreal · 2026
Nowcasting Inflation in Brazil Using Web Data — International Symposium on Forecasting · Charlottesville · 2023
Real-Time Forecasting of COVID-19 Cases Across US Regions — International Symposium on Forecasting · Remote · 2020

title: João R. Leripio
text:
João R. Leripio

  
    Forecasting, Statistical Modeling & Data Science
  

  
    
       GitHub
    

    
       LinkedIn
    
  





  About

  
    I specialize in statistical modeling, forecasting, and applied data
    science.
  

  
    My work focuses on time series, alternative and unstructured data,
    and the design of models and indicators that support real-world
    decision-making. I also use data engineering and software development
    practices to turn analytical work into reliable, reproducible pipelines
    and continuously updated data products.
  

  
    I currently lead the Data Science and Modeling team at
    Kapitalo,
    a macro hedge fund based in Brazil.
  



  Latest talk

  
    Nowcasting When Predictors Keep Changing,
    presented at the 46th International Symposium on Forecasting.
    The talk explores how to produce reliable forecasts from
    high-dimensional datasets whose composition changes continuously
    over time.
    See all talks ↗
  



  R for Economic Research (2e)

  
    The second edition of R for Economic Research was released
    in September 2025. The book offers a practical guide to modern
    economic analysis, with a strong emphasis on data workflows,
    statistical modeling, time series, and forecasting. It is
    available online for free
    and can also be purchased on
    Amazon.
  



  Currently working on...

  
    A new book about how analysts can move beyond one-off analyses
    and build reliable, long-lived analytical projects. The book brings
    together practical lessons on organizing, automating, and deploying
    data pipelines and analytical products for applied research.
